steps.title: Create a container element with display: grid
steps.instruction: Create a CSS rule for a class named 'container' that sets display to grid.
steps.hint: Start with .container { } and add display: grid; inside the curly braces.
steps.expectedOutcome: A CSS rule for the .container class is created with display: grid;
successCriteria: The .container class rule exists and includes display: grid;
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created a CSS Grid container. This is the foundation for using grid layout.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've created a .container class with display: grid; inside it.
steps.feedbackWrong: The CSS rule for .container with display: grid; is missing or incorrect.

steps.title: Define grid columns using fixed pixel units
steps.instruction: Inside the .container rule, add a grid-template-columns property with three columns of 100px each.
steps.hint: Use the property grid-template-columns: 100px 100px 100px; to create three equal columns.
steps.expectedOutcome: The .container will have three columns, each exactly 100 pixels wide.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully defined three fixed-width columns using pixels.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but check that you've added grid-template-columns with three 100px values.
steps.feedbackWrong: Let's try again. Add grid-template-columns: 100px 100px 100px; inside the .container rule.

steps.title: Add grid items to visualize the layout
steps.instruction: Create a CSS rule for a grid item class named '.grid-item' with basic styling to make it visible in the grid.
steps.hint: Define a new CSS selector for grid items and add properties like background color and padding.
steps.expectedOutcome: A new CSS rule for '.grid-item' with visible styling properties will be added.
successCriteria: The CSS file contains a '.grid-item' selector with at least one styling property like background-color or padding.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created a grid item class with visible styling. This will help visualize how content fills the grid cells.
steps.feedbackPartial: You started the grid item rule, but make sure to include at least one styling property (like background-color or padding) to make the items visible.
steps.feedbackWrong: The grid item styling isn't complete yet. Create a CSS rule for '.grid-item' with properties that make the items visible in the grid.

steps.title: Introduce the fr unit for flexible columns
steps.instruction: Replace the pixel values in the grid-template-columns property with fr units to create flexible columns.
steps.hint: Change the fixed pixel values to fr units. For example, replace 200px 200px with 1fr 1fr.
steps.analogousExample:
/* Example: using fr units for flexible columns */
grid-template-columns: 1fr 2fr 1fr;
steps.expectedOutcome: The grid columns will now use flexible fr units instead of fixed pixels.
successCriteria: The grid-template-columns property uses fr units (e.g., 1fr 1fr or similar).
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully replaced the pixel values with fr units, making the columns flexible.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're using fr units in the grid-template-columns property.
steps.feedbackWrong: The grid-template-columns property should use fr units instead of pixel values. Try replacing the numbers with values like 1fr.

steps.title: Create equal-width columns using fr
steps.instruction: Update the grid-template-columns property to create three equal-width columns using the fr unit instead of fixed pixel values.
steps.hint: Replace the pixel values with fr units. For three equal columns, you can use three equal fr values.
steps.analogousExample:
/* Example: three equal columns using fr */
grid-template-columns: 1fr 1fr 1fr;
steps.expectedOutcome: The grid container will have three columns of equal width that flexibly distribute the available space.
successCriteria: grid-template-columns is set to use three equal fr units (e.g., 1fr 1fr 1fr).
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully updated the grid to use flexible fr units for equal-width columns.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're using three equal fr units (like 1fr 1fr 1fr) instead of the pixel values.
steps.feedbackWrong: The grid-template-columns property should use three equal fr units (e.g., 1fr 1fr 1fr) to create equal-width columns.

steps.title: Mix fr units with other units
steps.instruction: Update the grid-template-columns property to combine one fixed pixel column (200px) with two flexible columns using fr units (1fr each).
steps.hint: Replace the existing grid-template-columns value with a combination of px and fr units, like '200px 1fr 1fr'.
steps.analogousExample:
/* Example: mixing fixed and flexible columns */
grid-template-columns: 100px 2fr 1fr;
steps.expectedOutcome: The container will have three columns: one fixed-width column of 200px and two equal flexible columns that share the remaining space.
successCriteria: grid-template-columns property contains both 'px' and 'fr' units in a single value.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully combined fixed and flexible units in your grid layout.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're using both 'px' and 'fr' units together in the grid-template-columns value.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check that you're updating the grid-template-columns property to include both pixel and fr units.

steps.title: Create a responsive sidebar layout
steps.instruction: Update the grid-template-columns property to create a sidebar layout with a fixed 250px sidebar and a flexible main content area using fr units.
steps.hint: Use a combination of a fixed pixel value and the fr unit. The first column could be the sidebar, and the second column the main content.
steps.analogousExample:
/* Example: sidebar layout with fixed sidebar and flexible main area */
grid-template-columns: 200px 1fr;
steps.expectedOutcome: The grid container will have two columns: a fixed-width sidebar and a flexible main content area that fills remaining space.
successCriteria: grid-template-columns property contains a pixel value (like 250px) and an fr unit (like 1fr)
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created a responsive sidebar layout using fr units alongside fixed pixels.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you have both a fixed pixel value and an fr unit in grid-template-columns.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check that you've updated grid-template-columns to include both a fixed pixel value and an fr unit.

steps.title: Add grid rows using fr units
steps.instruction: Add a grid-template-rows property to the .container class to define three rows with heights of 1fr, 2fr, and 1fr.
steps.hint: Use grid-template-rows: 1fr 2fr 1fr; to create three rows where the middle row is twice as tall as the others.
steps.expectedOutcome: The grid container will have three flexible rows with proportional heights.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added flexible rows using fr units. The middle row will be twice as tall as the top and bottom rows.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've added grid-template-rows with exactly three fr values: 1fr, 2fr, and 1fr.
steps.feedbackWrong: The grid-template-rows property is missing or incorrect. Add grid-template-rows: 1fr 2fr 1fr; to the .container class.

steps.title: Create a complex grid with both rows and columns
steps.instruction: Add a grid-template-rows property to the .container rule using fr units to define three rows of equal height.
steps.hint: Use grid-template-rows with three fr values, like 1fr 1fr 1fr, to create equal-height rows.
steps.expectedOutcome: The .container rule will have both grid-template-columns and grid-template-rows defined with fr units, creating a complete grid structure.
successCriteria: The .container rule includes a grid-template-rows property with three fr values (e.g., 1fr 1fr 1fr).
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've added grid-template-rows with fr units, creating a complete grid layout with both rows and columns.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure grid-template-rows uses fr units (like 1fr) and defines three rows.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check that you added grid-template-rows to the .container rule with three fr values (e.g., 1fr 1fr 1fr).

steps.title: Use minmax() with fr units for responsive constraints
steps.instruction: In the .container rule, update the grid-template-columns property to use minmax() with fr units: set the first column to minmax(150px, 1fr) and the second column to minmax(200px, 2fr).
steps.hint: The minmax() function takes two values: a minimum size and a maximum size. Combine it with fr units to create flexible columns with constraints.
steps.expectedOutcome: The grid columns will now have responsive constraints: the first column will be at least 150px and can grow up to 1fr, while the second column will be at least 200px and can grow up to 2fr.
successCriteria: The grid-template-columns property is updated to use minmax(150px, 1fr) and minmax(200px, 2fr).
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully used minmax() with fr units to create responsive grid columns with flexible constraints.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure both columns use minmax() with fr units. The first should be minmax(150px, 1fr) and the second minmax(200px, 2fr).
steps.feedbackWrong: That's not quite right. Update the grid-template-columns property to use minmax() with fr units as specified.
